body.statement: For every \(P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}\), any valid stopped-Hankel chart yields an equation \(L\bar v=\bar h\) with a unique solution in \(\mathcal A_O\). For every \((g,r)\in\mathcal G\), the resulting \(\pi^0_{g,r}\) equals the conditional law of \((Y_g(\infty),\ldots,Y_{g+r}(\infty))\) given \(G=g\), is invariant over the choice of valid chart and all legal non-permutation aliased realizations, and identifies \(\tau_{g,r}\). On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\), this invariant is evaluated by the displayed predeclared-coordinate formulas.
body.justification: The result identifies an entire cohort counterfactual law even when the latent transition and initial distribution are not identified.
body.gap: Weiss and Nadler characterize aliased parameter fibers, and Ishimaru identifies ATT by repeated measurements outside evolving staggered selection. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted latent-state likelihood, while Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside the parametric g-formula. None provides a stopped-law hazard operator or proves causal functional invariance on a legal non-permutation alias fiber.
body.consumer: Kim and Lee's binary VoD panel can replace observed-history extrapolation by a latent-state selection correction whenever the observable certificate passes.
